liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Black Peter** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls it the best Black Peter of the year; Reviewer loves this Black Peter as very focused [5][13]
- **Easy Wind** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out a good jam in Easy Wind; Easy Wind features sweet playing from Pigpen, and is a reviewer favorite [5][13]
- **Mason's Children** (2 reviews): The high vocal level makes Mason's Children even more enjoyable; Reviewer calls Mason's Children heavy and ranchy, among their all-time favorites [7][9]
- **Dancin' in the Streets** (2 reviews): Runs 14 minutes 52 seconds, goes into space and comes back; Reviewer hears raunchy, deep guitar from Jerry in a loose, juicy Dancing [8][15]
- **Saint Stephen** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer yelled for St. Stephen and the band played it; Notes list Pigpen on harmonica and Hammond B3 for St. Stephen [1][10]
- **Hard to Handle** (1 review): Reviewer especially likes this version of Hard to Handle [6]
- **Dire Wolf** (1 review): Reviewer likes the early working-out of Dire Wolf heard here [6]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-12-29.157581.sbd.anon.gems.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 132 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1969-12-29.sbd.cotsman.96143.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 133 min; rated 3.4/5 by 10 [2]. Said about its sound: Decent soundboard quality, with vocals mixed a little too high; thick keyboard runs are prominent [7]
- **gd69-12-29.sbd.8044.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 136 min; rated 4.17/5 by 12 [3]. Said about its sound: Rated roughly B+/A-: somewhat muddy with little hiss, and a small room ambience gives a sense of being there [4]

## Around the show

- Stage banter at the end of early tracks includes remarks that Bobby is buzzing and that there is nothing to see onstage [5]
- Reviewer believes the track order is wrong and gives a different first-set order, starting with China Cat and I Know You Rider [6]
- During the second Good Lovin', a man grabs the microphone and shouts a profane line about the microphone [8]
- The man with the microphone was yelling at the crowd to dance, then threw mic and stand into the audience [11]
- Reviewer's first Dead show: sat on the floor about 15 feet from the stage with a couple hundred people [10]
- This copy seems more complete than the shorter, incomplete version listed in the Taping Compendium [4]
- Reviewer is glad more recordings from the Boston New Year's Eve 1969 run are surfacing [7]
- Reviewer suspects an earlier commenter confused this show with the 31st [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-12-29.157581.sbd.anon.gems.flac16**: taped by Anon; transferred by Speed/pitch adjusted by Jason Chastain Mastering by Jim Blackwood, Jamie Waddell, and Steve Gravel Track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: Previously uncirculated SBD Vault Reel > Cassette > DAT [1]. Also: Transfer originally aired on Dead Legs program 20 on radiovalencia.fm, then was shared to shnflac.net in August 2022 [1]
- **gd1969-12-29.sbd.cotsman.96143.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by J. Cotsman; source: SBD>MR>C>D>CD [2]
- **gd69-12-29.sbd.8044.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Soundboard master reel (7-inch, 7.5 ips) transferred to DAT, then DAT, then CDR [3]
